tool_workspace.description: Upload your images below and click to invert their colors instantly.

requirements.intro: Inverting replaces every colour with its opposite on the colour wheel and flips light and dark: black becomes white, blue becomes yellow, red becomes cyan. The result looks like a film negative.

rows.label: 100% (default)
rows.value: A full negative. Inverting the result again gives you back the original image.
Every colour meets its opposite halfway, so the image turns into flat mid-grey.

rows.label: Between 0% and 50%
rows.value: A faded, washed-out look that keeps the original colours.

rows.label: Transparency
rows.value: Kept. Only the colours change; transparent areas of a PNG or WebP stay transparent.

how_to.title: How to invert an image
how_to.step1_text: Select or drag in one or more JPG, PNG or WebP files. They are processed in your browser and never uploaded.
how_to.step2_text: Leave the slider at 100% for a full negative, or lower it for a partial effect.
how_to.step3_text: Click the apply button. One image downloads directly; several download together as a ZIP.

items.q: Can I turn a photo negative into a normal photo?
items.a: Yes for black-and-white negatives: invert at 100% to see the positive. Colour negatives also have an orange film base, so the inverted result will look blue-tinted; it works as a preview but needs colour correction for a proper print.

items.q: Why did my image turn grey?
items.a: At 50% intensity every colour is pulled exactly halfway towards its opposite, which gives flat grey. Use 100% for a negative.
